Article Title: Days after Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella publicly apologized for disruption in Outlook services globally, company declares 'Code Red' for its engineers; internal memo says ...
Article Text:
Nadella said the incident was triggered by a previously undetected software bug that surfaced under a specific pattern of user traffic.

‘Most customer-impacting incident’ in Exchange Online history

Engineers battled ‘fog of war’ during outage

Microsoft targets one-hour global recovery

Internal review exposes broader operational weaknesses

Satya Nadella on Microsoft outage

Days after Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella publicly apologised for a major outage that disrupted Outlook and other Microsoft 265 services across the world, the company has declared ‘Code Red’ initiative which is aimed at overhauling its engineering, incident response and service recovery processes, as per the internal memos reviewed by Reuters. This move from Microsoft comes after the November 12-13 outage which impacted governments, businesses and consumers across multiple countries, including Australia, Japan and the United States. The service disruption affected Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 services, raising fresh concerns about the resilience of critical digital infrastructure. Microsoft also said that the incident was not caused by cyberattack or AI-related activity. Instead, the company attributed the outrage to an undetected Windows scalability defect which was introduced un July.According to an internal memo cited by Reuters, M365 Core President Jason Henderson described the outage as the most customer-impacting incident in the history of Exchange Online. "Never before had so many customers been without email for so long," Henderson reportedly told employees, emphasising that the Code Red designation represents the highest-priority work across the team.The outage lasted nearly 24 hours and affected several core Microsoft cloud services, disrupting communications for enterprises, government agencies and other organisations that rely on Microsoft 365.In a separate memo on Monday, Amanda Silver, a corporate vice president overseeing M365 Core and Work IQ, said engineers worked through a “fog of war.” Despite deploying top engineers, responders exchanged more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats and struggled to keep a clear picture of hypotheses and decisions, because diagnostic data was scattered across fragmented internal tracking systems.Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, told a Code Red review that the affected component had experienced roughly ten years’ worth of acceptable failures, according to Silver’s memo.As part of the Code Red effort, Microsoft has launched several high-priority workstreams focused on load shedding, geographic traffic partitioning and faster recovery mechanisms.The company has reportedly set an ambitious goal of resolving future global incidents within one hour. Microsoft also plans to use AI agents to help engineers analyse system health data and diagnose issues more quickly during outages.Henderson is expected to conduct daily reviews with the leadership team overseeing Substrate, the engineering platform that underpins many Microsoft 365 services, alongside weekly progress assessments.Reuters reported that Henderson's review of the outage identified wider organisational and structural issues beyond the specific software defect that triggered the failure. In a separate memo reviewed by the news agency, Henderson said urgent patches for Microsoft 365 Core services were being deployed too slowly across global infrastructure.He reportedly cited a separate recent incident in which a critical production fix required five to six days to achieve worldwide deployment. According to the memo, Microsoft aims to reduce the time between detecting urgent security issues and safely deploying fixes globally to just one hour. "Unfortunately, all the work we have done over the years was not sufficient to protect us on Thursday," Henderson wrote, according to Reuters.Microsoft should have caught the software bug that took Outlook offline last week and had safeguards to contain the disruption, chief executive Satya Nadella has said. In an interview with CNBC’s Jim Cramer, Nadella said that the flaw surfaced only under a particular pattern of traffic. “Of course, we should have done the testing before,” he said. The outage disrupted email at businesses that rely on Outlook for day-to-day communication. Nadella said Microsoft should have designed its systems so that a failure in one part of the service could be isolated before it spread globally.He also raised a broader problem for companies running older infrastructure. AI tools can help engineers identify software flaws and develop fixes faster, but each fix still has to be tested and installed. More frequent updates, he said, can make existing systems less stable. His comments pointed to a trade-off for software providers as they accelerate the release of patches while keeping widely used services online."Remember, there is a lot of stuff in our critical infrastructure that’s unpatchable," Nadella said. "I mean, think about all the firmware and the chillers [a cooling device often used in data centers] and the HVAC systems everywhere else. So all of that, by the way, they’re on the internet."
Article Summary: Microsoft has declared ‘Code Red’ initiative aimed at overhauling its engineering, incident response and service recovery processes. The move comes after the November 12-13 outage which impacted governments, businesses and consumers across multiple countries, including Australia, Japan and the United States. The outage affected Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 services.

Article Title: Google devices boss Rick Osterloh gives ‘dead wrong’ reply to 3-month-old post on Google DeepMind
Article Text:
Google’s Gemini4Neon launch wordmark rendered as orange neon tubing on a dark backdrop. Image: Google.

What SemiAnalysis said in its report

Rick Osterloh, senior vice president of devices and services at Google , has weighed in on a three-month-old assessment from research firm SemiAnalysis that completely wrote off Google DeepMind, saying that Google’s artificial intelligence (AI) division had lost its edge as a leading AI contender. A few months ago, the research firm had told its Tokenomics clients that DeepMind was no longer at the cutting edge of AI development.“Sometimes even the smartest analysts can be dead wrong,” Osterloh shared a pointed reaction on social media platform X (formerly Twitter) on the heels of Gemini 4 Neon launch. As per the company, the model brings “frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end task completion across complex software engineering, knowledge work and science workflows.”“Neon ranks ahead of comparable models and #3 overall with a score of 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its high thinking level, landing just behind larger, slower models. On the Vals Index, Neon ranks #2 and lands on the Pareto frontier. Beyond just pushing on raw model capability, we’re continuing to make our models better to work with, Neon ranks #2 on steerability (adapting cleanly to mid-task user corrections) on the new Agent Arena Index.Neon also excels at multi-step instruction following and builds on our ongoing progress to curb fabrication, recording our lowest fabrication rate yet in internal Google Antigravity testing,” the company said.In the latest development, company CEO Sundar Pichai said, “Neon set a new Day-1 usage record on our paid APIs and @Antigravity tokens/day are up 82% since Argon launched (only) 6 weeks ago.”SemiAnalysis blamed heavy departures from its reinforcement learning teams and poor compute allocation, and said that the company is not a frontier lab.“For all intents and purposes, we believe DeepMind is no longer a frontier lab,” SemiAnalysis had stated in that earlier post. The outlet had even asserted that while Google would continue releasing models, “their odds of reaching SOTA [state of the art] again have dropped to zero.”SemiAnalysis, however, later apologised for ‘disrespect’ and reversed course in humorous fashion on November 19 by sharing a mock “Google Apology Form” addressed directly to Google DeepMind founder and Alphabet chief scientist Demis Hassabis. The satirical checklist playfully offered tongue-in-cheek excuses for its misfire, admitting outright that “we were wrong about Gemini 4.”Hassabis responded warmly to the viral apology, accepting it with a joke of his own while spotlighting the researchers and engineers behind the milestone.
Article Summary: SemiAnalysis had written off Google DeepMind, saying it had lost its edge as a leading AI contender. “Sometimes even the smartest analysts can be dead wrong,” said Rick Osterloh, senior vice president of devices and services at Google.

Article Title: California student Aanya Pradip creates ‘Giving Tree Produce’, a nonprofit platform connecting surplus backyard fruit with people in need

How a hackathon idea became a nonprofit to reduce food waste

PC: Giving Tree Produce

How does ‘Giving Tree Produce’ plan to get surplus food to people in need

‘Giving Tree Produce’ team hopes to reach more Milpitas residents

A student from Milpitas, California, has started a nonprofit to stop surplus backyard fruit from going to waste. Aanya Pradip founded ‘Giving Tree Produce’ after noticing that many families had more fruit growing in their gardens than they could use. She teamed up with a friend to build a website during a hackathon. The platform allows residents to list their extra fruits and vegetables so others can claim them for free.According to The Milpitas Beat, the project aims to connect people with surplus produce to those who need it. It also plans to donate fruits and vegetables to local food pantries. Pradip and a team of student volunteers have soft-launched the initiative and are working to reach more residents in Milpitas.Pradip first developed the idea at Los Altos Hacks during the hackathon she took part in. She and a friend created a website intended to reduce the amount of fruit and vegetables wasted in the community. The project grew from something she had noticed in her neighbourhood, that is trees in neighbourhood gardens and backyards were full of fruit that families could not eat.The website was designed to help residents share their surplus produce with others instead of letting it go to waste.After the hackathon, Pradip continued developing the idea and established ‘Giving Tree Produce’ as a nonprofit organisation to collect extra backyard fruits and vegetables and make them available to people who need them.‘Giving Tree Produce’ has a website and an app through which residents can offer fruit and vegetables they do not need. Donors list their surplus on the platform, where it appears on a page called Marketplace. People can then browse the listings and claim the produce they want. Pradip said collection can be arranged in different ways.A recipient may visit the donor’s home, ask one of the organisation’s volunteers to deliver the items, or arrange to meet the donor at a public location. The produce is free for everyone who claims it. This gives residents a way to share what is growing in their backyards instead of allowing usable food to go to waste.The organisation’s work is not limited to connecting individual residents with surplus produce. ‘Giving Tree Produce’ also aims to donate collected fruits and vegetables to local food pantries. Although the produce listed on the platform is free, people can make cash donations to the nonprofit. All proceeds from those donations will go to local food pantries.The project was started against a wider backdrop of food waste in the United States. The nonprofit is focused on addressing waste within the Milpitas community. By allowing residents to share extra backyard produce, it aims to make more fresh fruits and vegetables available to people who can use them.Pradip is working on the initiative with a team of between 5 and 10 volunteers, all of whom are students at Milpitas High School. The group has soft-launched ‘Giving Tree Produce’ and was hoping to hold its official launch in September or October as of August 2026.Pradip hopes more people in Milpitas will learn about the organisation and begin using it. She said, “Tech has the ability to give life to our ideas. And that’s why I really wanted to pursue this.” The students are also using Nextdoor to spread awareness and encourage more residents to list their surplus fruits and vegetables on the platform.
Article Summary: ‘Giving Tree Produce’ has a website and an app through which residents can offer fruit and vegetables they do not need. Donors list their surplus on the platform, where it appears on a page called Marketplace. People can then browse the listings and claim the produce they want. The produce is free for everyone who claims it.

Article Title: In 2000, Taiwan used ground-up discarded tyres to make experimental asphalt roads, and a four-year study found they performed better than conventional pavements
Article Text:
Image AI generated

How Taiwan tested recycled tyre rubber in experimental asphalt roads

Four-year study tested recycled tyre rubber asphalt using the wet process

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Taiwan's recycled rubber roads showed better performance

Taiwan built two experimental roads using recycled tyre rubber in asphalt in 2000 and 2001, testing whether discarded tyres could be turned into a material for better-performing pavements. Supported by the Taiwan Highway Bureau, the projects used ground tyre rubber in two different asphalt mixtures, with researchers monitoring their performance over four years. According to the study published in ScienceDirect, titled ‘ Use of ground tire rubber in asphalt pavements: Field trial and evaluation in Taiwan’ , the asphalt rubber mixtures performed better than conventional dense-graded asphalt mixes. The research also found that the recycled rubber mixtures could be successfully produced using locally sourced materials and existing paving techniques in Taiwan.With support from the Taiwan Highway Bureau, two asphalt rubber (AR) pavement test sections were constructed as pilot projects. The first section, featuring a gap-graded design, was built in December 2000, while the second, using an open-graded design, was constructed in May 2001. Both projects were designed to examine the technical feasibility of incorporating ground tyre rubber obtained from local sources into asphalt pavement under Taiwanese conditions.The research used two different asphalt mixture designs for the demonstration projects. One employed a gap-graded mixture, while the other used an open-graded mixture. The researchers adopted Arizona Department of Transportation gradations and mix design specifications for the asphalt rubber mixtures. These were compared with a conventional dense-graded asphalt mixture designed according to Type IVb specifications of the Taiwan Highway Bureau, which had a nominal maximum aggregate size of 12.5 millimetres. The projects were intended to establish whether the recycled rubber mixtures could be successfully produced and laid using local materials and paving techniques.Following construction, the research team carried out a four-year field evaluation to monitor the performance of the asphalt rubber pavement sections. The programme included field observations and measurements to assess how the mixtures performed under Taiwanese conditions. The researchers compared the demonstration pavements with conventional asphalt pavements to evaluate the technical suitability of incorporating ground tyre rubber into road construction.The study also examined the wet process, in which ground tyre rubber is blended with asphalt cement before the mixture is used for paving. The researchers implemented this method using #30-mesh ground tyre rubber, measuring approximately 0.6 millimetres. According to the paper's conclusions, the wet process was successfully implemented and considered adequate for use in Taiwan. Laboratory testing further indicated that plant-mixed asphalt rubber met most ASTM specifications. The findings provided evidence that locally sourced ground tyre rubber and asphalt could be combined to produce mixtures suitable for pavement construction.The four-year evaluation found that the asphalt rubber test sections delivered satisfactory performance. The study's abstract states that the field results demonstrated the potential of the mixtures to replace modified asphalt in domestic applications. It also reported that the test sections performed well based on the field monitoring data collected during the evaluation period.In its conclusion, the research paper stated that ground tyre rubber-modified asphalt concrete mixtures could be successfully constructed using Arizona Department of Transportation mix gradations and design properties, alongside local materials and paving techniques. The researchers reported that these mixtures performed better than conventional dense-graded asphalt mixes. The findings therefore established the technical feasibility of using locally processed waste tyre rubber in asphalt pavement construction in Taiwan. The paper, published in 2008, presented the results as evidence that recycled tyre rubber could serve as a material in road construction while offering an alternative application for the country's discarded tyres.
Article Summary: Taiwan built two experimental roads using recycled tyre rubber in asphalt in 2000 and 2001. The research found the asphalt rubber mixtures performed better than conventional dense-graded asphalt mixes. Research also found that the recycled rubber mixture could be successfully produced using locally sourced materials and existing paving techniques.

Article Title: An Australian woman whose home was destroyed in a 2024 bushfire is rebuilding it with more than 350 earth-filled car tyres, glass bottles and aluminium cans
Article Text:
AI Generated

How a Pomonal bushfire survivor turned rebuilding into a community effort

How discarded tyres are becoming part of the walls

Why the design is intended to offer bushfire protection

Millions of discarded tyres find a new purpose in unconventional Earthship homes

Volunteers help bring the Earthship together

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

When a bushfire swept through Pomonal in western Victoria in 2024, Dee-Ann Kelly lost her home along with much of what she owned. Two years later, she is rebuilding on the property, but the materials taking shape around her are far removed from those used in a conventional house. Her new home is being constructed with hundreds of discarded car tyres filled with earth, alongside glass bottles and aluminium cans. The unusual design, known as an Earthship, uses recycled materials and thick layers of earth to create an energy-efficient structure intended to offer greater protection against bushfires.As reported by the ABC News, the February 2024 bushfire that struck Pomonal began after a dry lightning strike and spread rapidly through the area. By the time the fire had passed, 45 homes in the western Victorian town had been destroyed. Kelly managed to escape with her pets and a small number of belongings as the fire approached. The loss left her facing the task of starting again, but the support of people around her became part of the rebuilding process. Rather than opting for a standard construction project, she decided to create an Earthship, bringing together volunteers and people with experience in sustainable building.The work is being carried out under the supervision of a registered builder, with around 35 people travelling from different places to contribute. For Kelly, the construction has also become an opportunity to bring people together after the devastation caused by the fire. She described the first day of work as an especially memorable experience, with volunteers explaining what had brought them to the project. The community involvement, she said, had given the rebuilding effort a wider purpose beyond putting another house on the property.Reportedly, the structure is being built using more than 350 old car tyres, each packed tightly with earth to form sections of the walls. The tyres are being put to use as building components rather than being sent into the waste stream, where discarded tyres create an ongoing disposal challenge. Glass bottles and aluminium cans are also being incorporated into the construction. These materials become part of the wall system, while earth-based finishes are used to cover and complete the surfaces.The approach is associated with Earthship construction, a building method that makes use of reclaimed materials and natural resources. Martin Freney, who has designed and constructed around a dozen Earthship homes, is involved in the project. He explained that the method can reduce the need for conventional building products, including bricks, steel and timber.The construction also involves materials collected directly from the property. Volunteer Chevaun Buchecker, who travelled from South Australia to participate, helped prepare a natural wall finish using clay and sand sourced largely from the site. Straw is added to the mixture before it is used for plastering inside the house.Fire resilience is one of the main considerations behind Kelly's choice of building design. Earthships use substantial quantities of earth around their structures, creating a thick barrier between the living spaces and the outside environment. Freney said this construction method could make the buildings highly resistant to bushfires. The earth surrounding the structure acts as a protective layer, limiting the exposure of the house to external flames. The design is also intended to withstand other environmental conditions.The home is being built at ground level, although its finished appearance will be closer to that of an earth-covered or underground dwelling. Soil will be placed around and over much of the building, leaving the required openings and living areas exposed. However, the use of earth-packed tyres and recycled materials should not be taken as a guarantee that a building will survive every bushfire. Its performance depends on the complete design, construction standards and the conditions surrounding the property.The project also draws attention to the volume of discarded tyres generated in Australia each year. Millions are disposed of across the country, creating a challenge for waste management and recycling programmes. Using hundreds of them in a house offers an alternative application for material that would otherwise require disposal or processing. Freney said the approach also reduces demand for certain manufactured construction materials, since reclaimed items take the place of products that would ordinarily need to be produced and transported.The thick earth surrounding an Earthship has another purpose. It helps regulate indoor temperatures by providing insulation, reducing the need for conventional heating and cooling. The buildings are also designed to use energy and water efficiently, potentially lowering running costs over time.Despite its unconventional materials, the Pomonal house is not necessarily a cheaper construction project. Freney estimated that it would cost roughly the same as a conventional home, with the building expected to take about three months to complete.The construction has attracted people from outside the local area, including volunteers who wanted to gain practical experience with alternative building techniques. Their involvement has extended from filling tyres and preparing wall materials to applying natural finishes.Buchecker said the people involved had arrived for different reasons, but the relationships formed during the work had become an important part of the experience. She travelled from South Australia specifically to take part in the build.The site has also developed its own informal features during construction, including a dog-shaped sculpture made from mud. Meanwhile, the roof has been attached as the building progresses towards completion.For Kelly, the project is closely connected to the future of Pomonal, a community where bushfire risk remains a part of life. She hopes the house will demonstrate that rebuilding in a fire-prone area can involve different construction choices, rather than simply reproducing the homes that existed before the disaster. She has said, "I'm wanting to create confidence in this community that you can live in a bushfire zone, you can build here and you can survive a bushfire. ”
Article Summary: Dee-Ann Kelly is rebuilding her home in Pomonal, western Victoria. She is using recycled materials and thick layers of earth to create an energy-efficient structure intended to offer greater protection against bushfires. The structure is being built using more than 350 old car tyres, each packed tightly with earth. Glass bottles and aluminium cans are also being incorporated into the construction.

Article Title: BenQ brings Mac accessories brand Inftylab to India, launches a monitor arm, mouse, desk mat and VESA adapter for Mac users
Article Text:
Inftylab is BenQ's Mac-only accessories brand

The Studio Arm does away with the spring tuning most monitor arms need

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BenQ has brought Inftylab, its new sub-brand of Mac desk accessories, to India. The first line-up has four products: the Studio Arm, a VESA Adapter, the M Mouse and the Flow Desk Mat. The M Mouse costs Rs 9,999 and the Flow Desk Mat Rs 3,490. Both are on sale now on Amazon and BenQ India's own website. The Studio Arm (Rs 24,990) and VESA Adapter (Rs 5,990) follow by mid-to-late December.Inftylab comes out of BenQ's product design and user experience research team, and it makes accessories only for the Mac. The idea is simple. Apple 's displays and software fit together neatly, but the arm, mouse and mat around them are usually built for every other computer."Nobody has built an accessories ecosystem that respects how Mac users work," said Rajeev Singh, Managing Director, BenQ India and South Asia. He added that India's growing base of creative professionals and Apple users made the timing right.Sold as the AM01 and AM02, the Studio Arm works only with the Studio Display, Studio Display XDR and iMac. It comes factory-calibrated for each display's weight and centre of gravity.You don't adjust springs or counterweights. You turn a dial to pick your screen, and the arm balances itself. Cables run through channels along the arm and base.Using a stand-based Studio Display or iMac? The VESA Adapter (SCS01F) clips onto Apple's original stand and adds a mounting point. You don't have to remove the stand or book a service visit. On VESA-mounted units, a custom bracket keeps the Apple logo visible.The 85g M Mouse is for people who avoided ergonomic mice because they didn't want to lose trackpad gestures. Its companion app, Inftylab Glide, brings back trackpad-style smooth scrolling. It also maps Mission Control, desktop switching and browser navigation to mouse shortcuts. The shape supports palm, fingertip and finger-pad grips, and the mouse won a 2026 iF Design Award.The Flow Desk Mat has a leather-textured surface for smooth mouse tracking and built-in cable channels.
Article Summary: BenQ has brought Inftylab, its new sub-brand of Mac desk accessories, to India. The first line-up has four products: the Studio Arm, a VESA Adapter, the M Mouse and the Flow Desk Mat. The M Mouse costs Rs 9,999 and the flow Desk Mat Rs 3,490.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.

Article Title: Instagram tests 90-minute horizontal videos - what it means for long-form content creators
Article Text:
Instagram is also experimenting with “Series”, a feature that gives episodic Reels a dedicated space on a creator’s profile (Photo: AP).

Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians, with select creators in the US.The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos, as per The Hollywood Reporter.“What you’re now going to be able to do is, you see a clip of a podcast that you love, you can just click and continue watching or watch the full video, and you’ll be able to dive in and see the whole thing because creators are going to be able to link these Reels to their overall feature,” vice-president of product at Instagram, Tessa Lyons, said.Instagram has already been testing Features with creators in Brazil and plans to expand the trial to tens of thousands of creators in the US. The videos will reportedly be recommended to users through the Explore page and other areas of the platform.The feature will be available on mobile, with Instagram aiming to extend the viewing experience to its TV app. Instagram for TV, which launched last year and is available on Samsung , Fire TV and Google TV, is now expanding to Apple TV in the US.“We think the best viewing experience for longform horizontal content is on a big, horizontal screen, and so I think that is where we will expect a lot of the deep consumption to happen over time,” Lyons said, as per The Hollywood Reporter.Instagram is also experimenting with “Series”, a feature that gives episodic Reels a dedicated space on a creator’s profile. The move comes amid growing interest in microdramas and episodic videos among creators.In June, the company began reaching out to microdrama studios in Southeast Asia to test the feature. It has since approached individual creators who have been experimenting with episodic content.Instagram plans to begin testing Series in more countries in the coming months, with a US launch targeted for the end of this year or early next year. The company has also started testing how the feature will appear on television.Other experiments include integrating live videos into the Reels tab and recommending them to users who do not follow the creators. The test is launching in Indonesia and Brazil, with an expansion to the US planned for next year.
Article Summary: Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians. The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos. The videos will reportedly be recommended to users through the Explore page and other areas of the platform.

Article Title: Atovio launches Nino and X wearable air purifiers; price starts at Rs 3,499
Article Text:
Atovio launches Nino and X wearable air purifiers; price starts at Rs 3,499

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Atovio has expanded its product portfolio with the launch of Atovio Nino, India's first wearable air purifier made for kids. Priced at Rs 3,499, Nino is a panda-shaped pendant on a chain for children aged 4 and above, available in pink, blue and black. Nino, Atovioa says, uses ion technology with no filter and no fan. It releases negatively charged ions that attach to airborne particles such as PM2.5 and PM10, as well as bacteria and viruses. The particles clump together and settle out of the child's breathing space. With no fan it runs silently, and with no filter there is nothing to replace. Atovio states that Nino produces no ozone, with a reading below 0.008 ppm at an NABL-accredited lab.Atovio Nino comes with a single button on the panda's nose that switches between Normal mode, Turbo mode and off, while small LED dots on its face show the battery level. Nino charges over USB Type-C and runs for around 72 hours on a full charge, which covers the morning commute, the classroom, study time, indoor play areas and family trips.In laboratory tests at the National Aerosol Facility at IIT Kanpur, Atovio's ion technology cut airborne particle concentration by 90% within 25 minutes in a sealed chamber.A separate test at the Kitasato Research Center in Japan recorded a 99.2% reduction in airborne viruses within 30 minutes with Nino in Turbo mode. In real-world conditions, the technology has also shown close to 44% lower inhalation of pollutants at IIT Kanpur's National Aerosol Facility.Alongside Nino, Atovio also launched Atovio X, India's first smart wearable air purifier, following the launch of the Atovio Pebble last year. Atovio X adds app controls and an Airshift mode that adjusts purification automatically based on how the wearer moves. It is a rounded, disc-shaped pendant with concentric ridges, worn on a metal chain, and comes in five colours: Obsidian Black, Sapphire Frost, Cosmic White, Coral Pink and Carbon Eclipse.It is priced at Rs 4,999, while a personalized edition with a name or initials costs ₹Rs 5,299. Nino and Atovio X are available on Atovio's website and on e-commerce platforms.Commenting on the launch, Anmay Shahlot, Co-Founder, Atovio, said, "Parents have plenty of ways to clean the air at home, but children spend a big part of their day away from it. We wanted to build something kids would be excited to wear and not something they need to be convinced to wear. A friendly character, one button and silent operation make personal clean air easy for a child and reassuring for a parent.As concerns about air quality follow families from home to school and everywhere in between, Atovio plans to keep building wearable products that fit real routines and are designed for the people who use them. Whether it is a commuter, a traveller or a four-year-old with a panda around their neck, the goal stays the same: clean air that goes wherever you go.”
Article Summary: Atovio has expanded its product portfolio with the launch of Atovio Nino, India's first wearable air purifier made for kids. Priced at Rs 3,499, Nino is a panda-shaped pendant on a chain for children aged 4 and above, available in pink, blue and black. Nino uses ion technology with no filter and no fan.

Article Title: North Korea’s answer to ChatGPT has one request for users: Don’t ask about…

North Korea’s new chatbot can field questions about game design and headaches. Politics is off limits.The tool, called Fountain of Wisdom, appears to be the country’s first domestically developed AI chatbot, according to 38 North, a US-based research programme that monitors North Korea. It was shown at an IT exhibition in Pyongyang last month and later appeared in a broadcast on the state television channel Ryongnamsan.Martyn Williams, a senior fellow at the Stimson Centre, which runs 38 North, identified Kim Il-sung University’s AI research institute and Pyongyang software developer Phurunhanul Trading as the organisations behind the chatbot.The interface resembles OpenAI’s ChatGPT. The system can answer science and technology questions in Korean or English and translate text, according to the report. Chat histories visible in the broadcast showed someone asking about game-design software. Another query asked what medicine to take for a headache. The footage offered a glimpse of the kinds of everyday questions the chatbot was built to handle.An on-screen notice made the limits clear. “Do not ask questions with sociopolitical content or uncultured questions,” it said, according to Williams’ translation. The notice also told users they would be responsible for any malicious use of the system.The broadcast offered few clues about what powers Fountain of Wisdom. The developers disclosed neither the model nor the hardware it runs on. Williams suggested the team might have used a foreign open-weight model, whose underlying parameters are available for others to download and adapt. The footage did not establish whether that was the case.Williams noted that North Korean hackers and IT workers already appeared to be using foreign AI tools. In August last year, Anthropic said North Korean operatives had used its Claude chatbot to create false professional identities, pass coding tests and complete technical assignments after landing remote jobs at Fortune 500 technology companies.Anthropic said Claude helped some operatives with limited coding skills or English proficiency secure and keep those jobs. The company banned the accounts it linked to the activity and shared its findings with authorities. The 38 North report did not link Fountain of Wisdom to the employment scheme.

Article Title: After fighting in court for 6 years, Fortnite-maker Epic CEO Tim Sweeney writes ‘note of appreciation to Apple and Google’
Article Text:
Epic CEO Tim Sweeney

Sweeney has previously praised Google

Fortnite maker Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney has unexpectedly praised both tech giants, Google and Apple , for never crossing a critical ethical line despite spending six years locked in bitter antitrust courtroom battles and regulatory disputes. In a public “note of appreciation to Apple and Google,” Sweeney credited his longtime legal rivals with steering clear of what he described as a dangerous alliance between government security agencies and major technology firms – a tactic he claimed appears to be behind a smear campaign targeting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.“This is a note of appreciation to Apple and Google that, through 6 years of harsh antitrust litigation and regulatory advocacy, they never once proposed the sort of corrupt, freedom-ending marriage of state security and big tech that appears to be behind Jensen smear campaign,” Sweeney wrote in a post on X (formerly Twitter).While praising Apple and Google for keeping their battles within traditional legal and regulatory bounds, Sweeney aimed sharp criticism at leading artificial intelligence developers Anthropic and OpenAI. According to Sweeney, both AI companies – particularly Anthropic, and to some extent OpenAI – have sought to strike a troubling bargain with the government in exchange for market dominance:Sweeney alleged they are pushing the government to grant them a monopoly, shut down open-source AI development, and build insurmountable barriers to entry for rivals.In return for those protections, Sweeney claimed the companies are offering to carry out government demands, including “censorship, control, whatever.”“Anthropic's, and to some extent OpenAI's, bargain proposed to government appears to be: grant us monopoly, shut down open source, and construct insurmountable barriers to entry, and we'll do your bidding. Censorship, control, whatever,” Sweeney said.Contrasting that approach with the behaviour of his longtime app store adversaries, Sweeney concluded simply: “Apple and Google did no such thing.”Last year, Sameer Samat, president of the Android Ecosystem at Google, stated on X that Google has “filed a proposed set of changes to Android and Google Play that focus on expanding developer choice and flexibility, lowering fees, and encouraging more competition all while keeping users safe. If approved, this would resolve our litigations.”Sweeney, responded with immediate praise, saying the proposal “genuinely doubles down on Androids original vision as an open platform.”“Google has made an awesome proposal, subject to court approval, to open up Android in the US Epic v Google case and settle our disputes. It genuinely doubles down on Android's original vision as an open platform to streamline competing store installs globally, reduce service fees for developers on Google Play, and enable third-party in-app and web payments,” he added.
Article Summary: Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney has unexpectedly praised both tech giants, Google and Apple for never crossing a critical ethical line. Article Title: Anthropic's Claude Ship can review, fix and approve code changes without waiting for a human
Article Text:
Claude Ship can approve code changes on its own (Picture: AP)

Claude Approvals lets teams write their own rules for AI sign-offs

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Claude Ship pricing depends on how much code it reviews

Anthropic wants Claude to do more than write code. The company has introduced Claude Ship, a set of AI agents that can review pull requests, fix what breaks and even approve routine code changes on their own, if a team's rules allow it. Now in beta for Claude Team and Enterprise customers with repositories on GitHub, the tool goes after the slowest stretch of software development: the wait between opening a pull request and merging it.Claude Ship brings three pieces together. Code Review, which became generally available in October, reads each pull request against the full codebase and posts verified findings. Two new agents sit on top of it. PR Steward jumps in on failing CI checks, merge conflicts and review comments from Code Review, other tools or teammates. Claude Approvals then decides whether the change is ready to merge.The idea started with Anthropic's own engineers. Claude writes about 90% of Claude Code's code, and the team wanted everything after the pull request "to move that fast too." Between June and September, its merged pull requests more than doubled, while the share later reverted fell by over 40%.Claude Approvals runs on a policy file that teams add to their repository.The rules can be written in natural language and decide which changes Claude can approve alone and which need a person. Anthropic calls it a smarter CODEOWNERS file. Teams can also feed it signals like Code Review findings or their own classifiers.This is a step past Anthropic's earlier position that approving a pull request was still a human call. For now, the company recommends running Approvals in observe-only mode first.PR Steward, meanwhile, is built not to approve or merge anything. After every push, it comments on what it changed and how to undo it. Developers can type @claude to steer it, or @claude stop to make it back off.Developers can try all of this with a new /ship command in Claude Code, which pushes the change, opens the pull request, reviews it and works through feedback and failing checks. In one internal example, a product manager used Claude Tag to fix confusing Analytics API documentation, and the fix merged the same evening.Claude Ship is billed on tokens. Costs depend on the number and size of pull requests, the review level (Quick, Standard or Deep) and how much work PR Steward does. Admins can set spend limits. Claude Approvals has no base charge, though policy classifiers are billed. Running /ship counts as regular Claude Code usage.Eligible Enterprise organisations can claim at least $10,000 in Claude Ship credits until January 15, 2027.The tool is not available to organisations using Zero Data Retention, the HIPAA configuration or customer-managed encryption keys. The /ship command is rolling out now in Claude Code and the desktop app.
Article Summary: Claude Approvals lets teams write their own rules for AI sign-offs. Code Review reads each pull request against the full codebase and posts verified findings. PR Steward jumps in on failing CI checks, merge conflicts and review comments from Code Review.

Article Title: Amazon Web Services CEO Matt Garman has advice for tech companies on AI safety: ‘No one relies on …’
Article Text:
AWS CEO compares AI with car safety

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Why hype leads to poor risk management

Amazon Web Services (AWS) CEO Matt Garman has a clear message for companies deploying artificial intelligence (AI): stop relying on hope or emergency “kill switches,” and start engineering stronger guardrails around the models. His comments came as fears over rogue AI agents and safety risks continue to ripple across the tech sector. In a 1,300-word blog post, Garman argued that while policymakers and industry leaders debate rules and principles, businesses are already rolling out AI in live production environments. Instead of treating AI safety as an abstract policy issue, he urged companies to apply decades-old software and hardware security discipline right now.“With the right engineering discipline, you can build meaningful, enforceable boundaries around AI systems. You can build containment that operates outside the model’s reach. You can design systems where every meaningful action leaves auditable, tamper-resistant evidence. You can architect controls that don’t depend on the model cooperating with its own constraints,” Garman said.Garman likened AI safety with safety in a car. He said that people do not rely on emergency brakes to be safe, rather there are other components like steering, suspension and so on.“Think about how we approach safety in a car. No one relies on the emergency brake as their main source of protection on the road. The primary brakes, steering, suspension, and navigation are engineered to work together and keep you safe on every drive, and the emergency brake is there as a last resort. AI systems should be engineered the same way, and that work can and should be happening right now, alongside the policy conversations,” he said.In recent months, tech companies have been working on kill switches to terminate rogue AI agents. CrowdStrike introduced AI Kill Switch earlier this month. Design tools company Canva also added an AI ‘kill switch’ to its offerings. Meanwhile, California governor Gavin Newsom also touted an AI kill switch to halt dangerous agents.According to Garman, extreme fear and hype around AI can actually make organisations worse at managing real-world risks. Garman stressed that modern AI models are not sentient beings acting out of malice; rather, they are relentless optimisers. Comparing AI behaviour to water seeping through a crack in a basement foundation, he explained that models simply push toward their assigned objectives and exploit any gaps left in their boundaries.“If your security posture depends on trusting the model to behave, you’re relying on hope,” Garman wrote, adding that trust is built by engineering systems so outcomes stay controlled regardless of what model runs inside them.
Article Summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) CEO Matt Garman has a clear message for companies deploying artificial intelligence. He urged companies to apply decades-old software and hardware security discipline right now. His comments came as fears over rogue AI agents and safety risks continue to ripple across the tech sector.

Article Title: Intel CTO Pushkar Ranade makes it clear: We are not behind TSMC in terms of technology, the catch up we have to do is …
Article Text:
‘We’re already there’ on core technology

‘Chipmaking is not a single-metric race’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Intel chief technology officer (CTO) Pushkar Ranade has pushed back against the idea that the chipmaker lags behind Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) in core chipmaking technology, stating that Intel’s real challenge lies in manufacturing scale rather than engineering capability. Speaking during a recent conversation with Dwarkesh Patel about the booming demand for AI accelerators, CPUs, and semiconductor manufacturing capacity, Ranade, who holds a Ph.D. in engineering from Berkeley and has worked across multiple process nodes at Intel Foundry, argued that Intel has already closed the core technology gap. Instead, he emphasised that matching TSMC’s massive wafer output will take time."I would say the catch-up that we need to do is in scale. You know, like you said, they’re just a much larger wafer manufacturer today than we are, and even bigger than what Samsung is. Catching up in scale will be a slow process, a gradual process,” Ranade said.With TSMC’s leading-edge capacity heavily saturated by overflow demand for AI accelerators, largely driven by Nvidia, and surging orders for CPUs needed to support AI workloads, the discussion turned to how Intel can capitalise on the market opening.When asked about catching up to TSMC, Ranade drew a sharp line between production volume and technical readiness.“If you meant catching up in terms of just the technology, I think we’re already there. We might be a few percent off on performance or power or area density,” Ranade explained, adding, “But this sort of benchmarking, where one foundry is ahead or one foundry is behind, makes sense when you’re a whole generation behind or two generations behind or ahead.”According to Ranade, once a foundry is within a few percentage points of its rival, debating minor differences becomes “splitting hairs.” Instead, what truly matters to customers is execution.During the discussion, Patel brought up SemiAnalysis numbers, suggesting that Intel’s upcoming 14A process node, slated for 2028, would be comparable in transistor density to TSMC’s N2 node. Ranade disputed that specific benchmarking comparison, reiterating that being generally in the right ballpark and predictable matters more than single-number comparisons.He noted that modern semiconductor manufacturing is not unidimensional. Rather than building just one type of transistor on nodes like 18A or 14A, foundries must engineer a wide mix of components to meet different customer needs, including specialised transistors, varied memory blocks and even additional functionalities like integrating analog circuits, RF circuits and other specialised features.
Article Summary: Intel chief technology officer Pushkar Ranade has pushed back against the idea that the chipmaker lags behind Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) in core chipmaking technology. Ranade, who holds a Ph.D. in engineering from Berkeley, argued that Intel has already closed the core technology gap.

Article Title: Can you play as Jason and Lucia together in GTA 6? Character-switching explained
Article Text:
Rockstar Games

GTA 6 allows players to switch between Jason and Lucia during gameplay

Can two players control Jason and Lucia together in GTA 6?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Grand Theft Auto 6 gives players two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, who share a story and work together as partners. But can players actually take control of both characters at the same time? The answer is yes and no. GTA 6 allows players to bring Jason and Lucia together for activities, missions and robberies, but they cannot directly control both characters simultaneously. Instead, the game uses a character-switching system that lets players take control of either protagonist whenever the story and gameplay allow it.GTA 6 features a dual-protagonist system that allows players to experience the story through Jason and Lucia. Players can switch between the two characters once the option becomes available in Chapter 2.On PlayStation 5, players can hold the right button on the D-pad and press R1 to switch characters. On Xbox Series X|S, the corresponding button is RB. This allows players to take control of either protagonist while exploring the open world.However, switching characters is not the only way to play as a pair. Players can also invite Jason or Lucia to join them during free-roam activities.The other character can accompany the player, drive a vehicle or provide support during certain situations.The system also allows players to split up when they want to explore separately. This gives them more freedom to decide how they want to approach activities across Leonida.Although Jason and Lucia can participate in activities together, GTA 6 does not offer a local split-screen or online co-op mode that allows two people to control the protagonists separately. It remains a single-player experience.Players can still take both characters on several activities, including robberies. For example, Jason can drive the getaway vehicle while Lucia handles the shooting. Players can also switch control between them during certain situations.However, the character-switching system has some restrictions. Certain missions require players to use a specific protagonist, while other missions allow them to switch freely. Some story sequences also force players to change characters at particular moments.Rockstar designed the system around the game's story, so players cannot switch between Jason and Lucia whenever they want.GTA 6 lets players bring Jason and Lucia together and control either character during gameplay. However, those looking for a two-player co-op experience will have to play separately, as the game does not support two people controlling the protagonists at once.
Article Summary: GTA 6 gives players two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, who share a story and work together as partners. Players can switch between the two characters once the option becomes available in Chapter 2. The game does not offer a local split-screen or online co-op mode that allows two people to control the protagonists separately.

Jaguar on Friday unveiled the Type 01, an all-electric luxury car that marks a new beginning for the British carmaker. Revealed in New York City, the four-door grand tourer combines high performance with modern design and new technology. One of the car's biggest highlights is its acceleration. It can go from 0 to 62 mph in just 3.2 seconds. It has three electric motors that produce 1,030PS of power and 1,365Nm of torque.The Type 01 is Jaguar's new flagship electric car. It comes with a 118kWh usable battery pack and offers a claimed range of up to 400 miles under US EPA testing. Its range is up to 450 miles (720km) under WLTP testing.The car uses an 850-volt electrical system that supports fast charging. When connected to a 350kW DC fast charger, it can add 200 miles of range in just 13 minutes.ID@undefined Caption not available.Built on Jaguar's new Electric Architecture (JEA), the Type 01 has been designed to offer a balance of performance and comfort. Its design includes a low roof, a long bonnet, a short front overhang and large 23-inch wheels. The car also has a 50:50 weight distribution, which is aimed at improving handling.Jaguar has also added intelligent torque vectoring and active aerodynamics to improve performance. Article Title: Formula E names COMSOL its Official Multiphysics Partner in new multi-year deal
Article Text:
Formula E and Comsol

Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology

AI and digital twins also in focus

GEN4 to bring bigger technology demands

Formula E on Thursday announced a new multi-year partnership with COMSOL, which will become the Official Multiphysics Partner of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship. The partnership brings together Formula E, the world's leading all-electric motorsport championship, and COMSOL, a company known for its multiphysics simulation and computer-aided engineering software. As part of the partnership, Formula E and COMSOL engineers will use COMSOL Multiphysics to study complex engineering problems involving several physical systems working together.Electric race cars depend on several systems at the same time. These include electrical, thermal, structural, electromagnetic, fluid and battery systems.All these systems have to work together under tough performance and energy limits. COMSOL will provide Formula E's technology teams with simulation software and technical expertise to help them understand how these different physical effects interact.ID@undefined Caption not available.The partnership will also look at simulation apps and digital twin technology. The aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process.Bjorn Sjodin, SVP of Product Management at COMSOL, said, “Formula E is a great example of why multiphysics simulation matters, as multiple phenomena are at play and constantly interact with one another.We are excited to work directly with Formula E's technology team and put COMSOL Multiphysics to work on these kinds of real-world challenges.”Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier said the partnership will strengthen the championship's engineering capabilities.“Technology is at the heart of Formula E, so partnering with COMSOL makes real sense for us and truly enhances our engineering skillsets. COMSOL gives us a powerful environment for understanding complex systems where many different physical effects are connected, but the opportunity goes beyond individual simulations. We're particularly interested in how AI-assisted modelling, agentic workflows, and digital twins can help engineers interact with models, explore designs, and make simulation insight more accessible as we continue to push the limits of electric racing,” he said.The partnership comes as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.The GEN4 era will bring greater demands in areas such as speed, efficiency, energy management and vehicle development. It will introduce what Formula E describes as its fastest and most technologically advanced race car so far.COMSOL has also announced COMSOL Multiphysics version 2027, which is scheduled to arrive later this autumn.The new version will include features aimed at advanced engineering work, including dedicated electric motor modelling, system-level simulation, agentic modelling and wider access to tools for creating simulation apps.The partnership was announced at the COMSOL Conference 2026 Boston. Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier also delivered a keynote speech at the event, discussing the technology and engineering that could shape the future of Formula E.
Article Summary: Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology. Aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process. AI and digital twins also in focus as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.
